claim_text: GoFundMe says an unauthorized third party accessed data from the GoFundMe Pro API on Oct 10 to 18 and on Nov 8 to 9, 2026
summary: GoFundMe's Nov 20 security notice says it "identified a security incident of unauthorized third-party access to our customer platform, GoFundMe Pro", with access to "certain data from the GoFundMe Pro API" on those dates.
detail: It says it disabled unauthorized accounts, brought in outside cybersecurity professionals and reported the matter to law enforcement. The notice calls the investigation ongoing. GoFundMe says it has "addressed the known methods of unauthorized access", which is not the same as saying how the attacker got in.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A Tier 1 source, GoFundMe's own status-page notice, admits the access, and independent outlets report the same statements.

claim_text: DonorPerfect says it found unauthorized activity on its systems and took DonorPerfect offline
summary: DonorPerfect's Nov 11 status update refers to the unauthorized activity under investigation; on Nov 10 it took the application offline as a precaution. Fortune reports the company confirmed it.
detail: DonorPerfect's status page on Nov 11 says its "cybersecurity investigation is also continuing to determine the full scope of the unauthorized activity, including what customer information may have been affected." On Nov 10 it said it was taking the application offline "out of an abundance of caution". Fortune reports the company confirmed unauthorized activity involving certain systems. DonorPerfect has not published what the activity was beyond statements to press (see the AI bots claim). A third-party forensic firm is still investigating, per Fortune. An undated customer message on DonorPerfect's own website says: "We confirmed unauthorized activity involving certain DonorPerfect systems." It says the investigation included assessing whether customer information was accessed, and that confirmed findings will go directly to affected organizations.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Tier 1 sources, DonorPerfect's own status page and its customer message, confirm unauthorized activity, and Fortune reports the same.
notes: DonorPerfect also contacted the FBI, per the Chronicle of Philanthropy as cited by Fortune; the FBI would not say whether it is investigating.

claim_text: GoFundMe says the data taken included names, postal addresses, phone numbers and, for some people, dates of birth
summary: The Nov 20 notice says the data "included limited personal information such as names, postal addresses, phone numbers and, for some, dates of birth or other information provided voluntarily in registration forms."
detail: Fortune, citing GoFundMe's email to affected customers, also lists email addresses. The public notice we read does not list them. How many people are affected has not been published.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: GoFundMe's own notice (Tier 1) states what was accessed.

claim_text: GoFundMe says donor and supporter credentials, full card numbers, security codes and bank details were not accessed
summary: The notice says "at this time, donor and supporter credentials were not accessed" and that "no full card numbers, security codes or bank account details stored by GoFundMe Pro were accessed."
detail: This is the company's own statement of what was not taken, while its investigation is still running, and the words "at this time" leave it open. We found no independent check.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Only GoFundMe states it, and it can change as the investigation continues.

claim_text: For some organizations, the attacker also took credentials for the GoFundMe Pro Salesforce integration and may have used them to reach those organizations' Salesforce records
summary: Press quoting GoFundMe's message to customers says the attacker took credentials for the Salesforce integration and may have used them to reach some organizations' Salesforce records.
detail: The Chronicle of Philanthropy and Fortune quote GoFundMe's message to customers saying the attacker "accessed credentials associated with the GoFundMe Pro Salesforce integration, which they may have used to access those organizations' records in Salesforce." GoFundMe told Salesforce users to rotate all stored keys and credentials and review account activity. We found this wording in press coverage of the customer message, not on a public GoFundMe page. How many organizations, and whether any Salesforce records were actually reached, is not published.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets quote the same company message; no official public page found.

claim_text: GoFundMe Pro's connection to Salesforce was cut off, and GoFundMe says it remains disabled
summary: GoFundMe's status page reports data failing to sync to Salesforce from Nov 9.
detail: On Nov 20 it says the GoFundMe Pro packages in Salesforce were restored but "the connection between GoFundMe Pro and Salesforce remains disabled" and customers should not reconnect yet. The status page does not itself say the shutdown was a security step; Salesforce's own advisory (c007) does, and on Nov 20 Salesforce also says the connected apps remain disabled.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: GoFundMe's own status page (Tier 1) gives the dates and current state.

claim_text: Salesforce says it disabled the GoFundMe Pro connected app over suspicious use of access tokens, and that this was not a flaw in Salesforce
summary: Salesforce says on its own public status page that it disabled the GoFundMe Pro connected app as a precaution after suspicious use of access tokens, and that the problem was not a flaw in Salesforce.
detail: Salesforce's Trust status advisory, posted Nov 11 (12:27 PM ET), says it "disabled the GoFundMe Pro connected app and associated managed packages as a precaution after identifying suspicious use of access tokens associated with the third-party provider" and that "the issue did not arise from a vulnerability within the core Salesforce platform." The same words were quoted in The NonProfit Times. In an update on Nov 20 (4:30 PM ET), Salesforce says it re-enabled the GoFundMe Pro managed packages, but the connected apps stay disabled until GoFundMe completes security remediation and shows the integrations can be restored safely. Salesforce says it will notify affected customers "without undue delay if we identify unauthorized access to their data"; it has not said it found any. That it was not a Salesforce flaw is Salesforce's own account; we found no independent review.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Salesforce's own public status advisory (Tier 1) states what it did and why; The NonProfit Times quotes the same statement.
notes: Moved from Reported to Confirmed on Nov 21 after we found Salesforce's own public advisory (s010). Confirmed covers what Salesforce says it did and said, not an independent finding that Salesforce was not at fault.

claim_text: DonorPerfect took its API offline on Nov 10, then the whole application that evening, and has restored most of it since Nov 14, but its API and mobile app were still unavailable on Nov 21
summary: DonorPerfect went offline Nov 10 and began staged restoration Nov 14. Most of it is back, but its API and mobile app were still unavailable on Nov 21.
detail: DonorPerfect's status page: API offline Nov 10 (3:12 PM ET); whole application offline Nov 10 (8:16 PM ET); public websites back Nov 12; Classic Online Forms donations back Nov 13; staged restoration of the application from Nov 14 (10:50 PM ET); on Nov 21 (9:31 AM ET) it says four partner integrations are rebuilt but not yet active, with activation starting Monday, Nov 23, and no reliable timeframe for the rest of the API. Fortune reports the company has about 11,000 customers and that donations through partners like GoFundMe are processed safely but do not pass into DonorPerfect automatically.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: DonorPerfect's own status page (Tier 1), with the dates in its updates.

claim_text: Whether DonorPerfect customer or donor data was taken, and how much
summary: DonorPerfect told The NonProfit Times it "do[es] not have a determination of who was impacted or what if anything was taken".
detail: Its Nov 11 status update says the investigation continues "including what customer information may have been affected." A third-party forensic firm is still working, per Fortune. No count of affected people has been published for either DonorPerfect or GoFundMe Pro. DonorPerfect's undated customer message says it will communicate confirmed findings directly to affected organizations; it does not say whether any data was taken.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The company itself says it has no determination yet.

claim_text: DonorPerfect attributes its attacks to AI bots, entering through its marketing website
summary: DonorPerfect's president told The NonProfit Times and Fortune the company has "a lot of evidence" the attacks used AI bots, that the initial access point was its marketing website, and that the root cause has been identified.
detail: An unnamed company official told the NonProfit Times an AI agent was "rapidly adapting its approaches". This is the company's claim to the press. It is not on the status page, and the forensic firm's findings are not out. We found no independent confirmation, and no outside expert reviewing the evidence.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets quote the company; nobody independent has checked it.
notes: Root cause is not closed until a published finding exists.

claim_text: The same attacker hit both GoFundMe Pro and DonorPerfect
summary: DonorPerfect says an unnamed technology leader told it of an attack by "the same bad actor" while it was already investigating.
detail: GoFundMe says there is "strong reason to believe that bad actors are making similar attempts to access other fundraising platforms." Neither company says it was the same attacker as the other, and the access dates differ. No official or independent finding ties the two together.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Similar timing and similar targets are not evidence of one attacker.

summary: Neither company, any law enforcement agency or any outlet we read names an attacker or says a group has claimed these attacks. We looked at news coverage and company pages only and did not visit any leak site, dark-web page or tracker.
detail: The NonProfit Times says the bots' IP addresses were all outside the United States but could have been rerouted to hide their location, citing no named source; we did not count that as attribution.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source names or claims an attacker.

claim_text: Funds were diverted from a fundraising platform in at least one case
summary: The NonProfit Times says an unnamed nonprofit technologist, speaking on background, told it funds were diverted from a platform in at least one case.
detail: It does not say which platform, and neither GoFundMe nor DonorPerfect says money was taken. GoFundMe says transaction processing is unaffected.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: One anonymous account in one outlet; nothing official or independent.

claim_text: GoFundMe began notifying affected people on Nov 19, with mailed notices and regulator filings in North Dakota and Washington
summary: The NonProfit Times reports GoFundMe is emailing "all involved individuals beginning on November 19, 2026", mailing notices in North Dakota and Washington and notifying those states' regulators, and has opened a call center.
detail: The notices do not name any nonprofit. Fortune also reports the Nov 19 start. We did not read the regulator filings themselves.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets report it from GoFundMe's statements; not read on a public GoFundMe or regulator page.

claim_text: These breaches are part of the November 2026 wave of outages
summary: Fortune lists the DonorPerfect incident alongside the Microsoft, FAA and Chase outages, then says DonorPerfect's was "different" because the company confirmed unauthorized activity.
detail: No source ties these two breaches to those outages. The access to GoFundMe Pro began in October.
label: Not established
notes: Other isitahack pages cover those outages.
